title: Waffle Wagon Coverage
subject: Evidence
stem:
At a city festival, Lydia’s privately owned “Loaves & Fishes” waffle trailer burned to the frame. Lydia was charged with arson. To show that Lydia had a motive to set the fire, the government offered proof that the trailer and its kitchen equipment were fully insured.

Should the court admit this evidence?
call: Should the court admit this evidence?

choices.A: Yes, because any conduct of a party to the case is admissible when offered against that party.
choices.B: Yes, because the insurance on the trailer and equipment has a tendency to show that Lydia had a motive to burn the trailer.
choices.C: No, because evidence of insurance is not admissible on the issue of whether the insured acted wrongfully.
choices.D: No, because the probative value of the insurance evidence on whether Lydia intentionally burned the trailer is substantially outweighed by the dangers of unfair prejudice and jury confusion.

rightExplanation: B is correct. The government is offering the insurance evidence for motive: Lydia had a possible financial reason to burn insured property. That is enough for relevance because the evidence tends to make a consequential fact more probable. Gold Key: insurance evidence is purpose-sensitive; it is not automatically excluded merely because the word “insurance” appears. Silver Key: lock the offered purpose first. Here the purpose is motive, not a blanket claim that insured people act wrongfully.

c3.label: CUT A — NOT_TRUE / tiered_absolute
c3.text: “Any conduct” is too broad. Cut on overclaim.

c3.label: CUT C — NOT_RESPONSIVE / bait_doctrine
c3.text: This is the familiar insurance-exclusion rule, but the choice uses the wrong purpose. The stem says motive. Cut on purpose mismatch.

c3.label: CUT D — NOT_RESPONSIVE / wrong_element
c3.text: This choice turns the case into a Rule 403 exclusion case without a fact showing substantial unfair prejudice or confusion. Cut because it elevates the wrong element.

c3.label: Residual
c3.text: B. It matches the stem’s purpose: motive.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: Not needed. Anchor support confirms the dominant trap.

studentScript: Purpose first. The government offers insurance to show motive. Cut the blanket party-conduct answer. Cut the insurance-is-out answer because it answers wrongful conduct, not motive. Cut the 403 answer because the stem gives no substantial-danger fact. Pick B.

A.signal: The word 'any' claims all party conduct is admissible.
A.lawyer: No Federal Rule creates a blanket rule admitting any conduct merely because it is offered against a party.

B.signal: The choice matches the stem's purpose: motive.
B.lawyer: FRE 401, 403, and 411 confirm admissibility for a relevant motive purpose absent substantial Rule 403 dangers.

C.signal: The choice says wrongful conduct; the stem says motive.
C.lawyer: FRE 411 is purpose-limited and permits insurance evidence for another purpose.

D.signal: The stem gives no fact showing the danger substantially outweighs motive value.
D.lawyer: FRE 403 requires substantial outweighing; the official explanation supplies no such danger.

goldKeys.statement: Insurance evidence is purpose-sensitive. It cannot be used merely to prove wrongful conduct, but it can be admitted when the offered purpose is a separate non-propensity point such as motive or financial incentive.
goldKeys.trigger: Insurance evidence offered to show why the accused would burn or damage insured property.
goldKeys.unlocks: The insurance-is-inadmissible trap when the stem offers insurance to prove motive.

silverKeys.statement: In Evidence, lock the offered purpose before judging the rule. The same insurance fact can be barred for one purpose and admitted for another.
silverKeys.trigger: The stem says the proponent offers insurance evidence to show motive.
silverKeys.unlocks: The dominant trap that treats an insurance rule as a blanket exclusion instead of a purpose-limited rule.

remediation.title: Insurance evidence: purpose first
remediation.signal: The stem offers insurance evidence and names a specific purpose.
remediation.studentMove: State the purpose before applying any exclusion.
remediation.tinyRule: Insurance is not a blanket exclusion; motive purpose can make it admissible.
